info.name: Gateway Service
info.description: The Gateway 4.0.0 (Lab 4, #110): every client request goes to the Message Broker as a gRPC Request, and only the client's routes are served; see docs/GATEWAY.md. Run against the team stack with the broker (#113). The task timeout and concurrent limit are not shown here: the /dev routes that gave a slow request are no longer Gateway routes; they are covered by the Gateway's tests and, for the broker's own 408/429, by its collection and scripts/smoke.py.

variable.description: A started session in Discord DMs with {{player_id}} in it (set by a shift run through Session, e.g. the Lab 4 shift collection of #113); empty skips the 201 ticket request

item.name: health, status and metrics
item.description: The Gateway's own routes: no credential, not tasks. `/metrics` is scraped by Prometheus as a static target (#113).

request.description: The status endpoint every service, Service Discovery and the Gateway share (CPR issue #71): `service`, `instance_id` (`gateway-<hostname>`), `version`, `status` (always `up`: the Gateway has no database), `in_flight` (requests holding a task slot right now) and `max_concurrent_tasks`. No credential; not a task, so it answers also while the concurrent task limit is reached. `GET /health` is unchanged.

item.name: routing through the broker
item.description: `{{base_url}}/api/v1/<prefix>/<rest>` reaches the service behind `<prefix>` as `/api/v1/<rest>`, and `/api/v1/<prefix>/health` as the service's own `/health` (docs/GATEWAY.md §5, §7). Since `4.0.0` every request goes to the Message Broker as a gRPC `Request` and the broker chooses the instance; the reply comes back unchanged. Needs the broker and the services of the Lab 4 stack.

item.name: The same path behind another prefix: /api/v1/credential/health

request.description: Only the prefix differs; the request reaches a different service.

`/api/v1/applicants/...` is the service's own path; through the Gateway it needs `/api/v1/applicant/` in front. No service is registered as `applicants`, so the Gateway answers itself, before any credential check, and `details.service` names the segment it did not recognise.

request.description: `..`, plain or percent-encoded, never reaches a service: the Gateway refuses the path itself.

item.name: The service's own error passes through unchanged

request.description: A 404 from Applicant Service, not from the Gateway: the code is the service's own (`APPLICANT_NOT_FOUND`), and status, headers and body arrive as the service wrote them. Compare with the Gateway's own 404 two requests up, whose code is `NOT_FOUND`.

item.name: X-Request-ID comes back on the Gateway's own errors too (401)

The same holds for every error the Gateway answers itself (400, 401, 403, 404, 408, 429, 502, 503, 500).

item.name: authorization
item.description: A player sends `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` (HS256 with JWT_SECRET, `sub` = the player's id). Every route that is not public takes it; the service token is no credential for a route any more (README Authentication, Lab 4). The collection signs the tokens itself from `{{jwt_secret}}`.

item.name: Player route without a credential (401 UNAUTHENTICATED)

request.description: `GET /applicants/{id}/documents` is player only. No token: refused before the service is called, so the applicant id does not even have to exist.

item.name: Player route with only a service token (401)

request.description: On a player-only route the service token is ignored: it does not identify a player.

item.name: Player token signed with another secret (401)

request.description: Well-formed, unexpired, but not signed with the Gateway's JWT_SECRET. Only Player Service holds that secret.
Correctly signed, `exp` an hour ago. The Gateway tolerates JWT_LEEWAY_SECONDS (5) of clock skew, no more.

request.description: Public routes need no credential and get none: the Gateway forwards them without a check, and strips `Authorization`, `X-Service-Token` and any `X-Player-Id` the caller sent, so nobody can pose as a player by setting the header themselves.

item.name: websocket negotiation (the Gateway negotiates, the client connects to Discord DMs directly)
item.description: `POST /api/v1/discord-dms/ws-tickets` is a player route through the broker; the client then opens `ws_url` on Discord DMs directly. The `201` request needs `ws_session_id`: a started session with `{{player_id}}` in it.

item.name: POST /api/v1/discord-dms/ws-tickets -> 201 with the direct ws_url and a one-time ticket

exec: pm.test('ws_url points at Discord DMS directly, with a one-time ticket', () => { pm.expect(b.ws_url).to.match(/^wss?:\/\/.+\/api\/v1\/ws\?ticket=[0-9a-f]{32}$/); pm.expect(b.ws_url.split('/api/')[0]).to.not.include(':8080'); });
pm.test('expires_at is about 30 s away', () => { const d = (new Date(b.expires_at) - Date.now()) / 1000; pm.expect(d).to.be.within(20, 31); });
console.log('open directly, once, within 30 s: ' + b.ws_url);
// Needs a started session in Discord DMs with {{player_id}} in it: Discord DMs learns sessions from
// session.started through the broker, so start a shift first (the Lab 4 shift collection of #113, or
// Session's own collection) and set ws_session_id. Without it this request is skipped.

request.description: The Gateway asks Discord DMs for the ticket on the player's behalf and hands the answer back; it never carries the chat. Open the printed ws_url with a WebSocket client (for example `wscat -c "<ws_url>"`).

item.name: GET /api/v1/player/logs - a service's logs are not a Gateway route

exec: pm.test('404 NOT_FOUND, answered by the Gateway', () => {
// Player tokens, signed the way Player Service signs them: HS256 with JWT_SECRET, `sub` = the
// player's id, `iat` and `exp`. The Gateway verifies the signature, so `jwt_secret` must be the
// JWT_SECRET of the Gateway being called (gateway-service/.env).
return header + '.' + payload + '.' + b64url(CryptoJS.HmacSHA256(header + '.' + payload, secret));
pm.collectionVariables.set('player_token', mint({ sub: sub, iat: now, exp: now + 3600 }, secret));
pm.collectionVariables.set('expired_token', mint({ sub: sub, iat: now - 7200, exp: now - 3600 }, secret));
pm.collectionVariables.set('foreign_token', mint({ sub: sub, iat: now, exp: now + 3600 }, 'not-the-secret-of-this-gateway-at-all'));
// Through the Gateway a player is identified by a JWT (HS256, JWT_SECRET shared with Player Service),
// never by X-Player-Id: the Gateway checks the token, discards any client-sent X-Player-Id and sets
// its own from the token's sub. Player Service's POST /api/v1/auth/login is not published yet, so
// this script signs the token itself: every request that names a player in X-Player-Id gets
// Authorization: Bearer <jwt> with sub = that id, and the X-Player-Id header is dropped.
// jwt_secret must equal JWT_SECRET of the Gateway in the stack's .env.
const unsigned = part({ alg: 'HS256', typ: 'JWT' }) + '.' + part({ sub: sub, iat: now, exp: now + 300 });
